# `transaction` commands

## `transaction find`

Find any transaction: search invoices, sales receipts, credit memos, statement charges, customer payments and refunds, estimates, proposals, work orders, purchase orders, item receipts, bills, bill payments, vendor credits, checks, card charges and credits, deposits, transfers, journal entries, sales tax payments and adjustments and inventory adjustments in one read, by any mix of type (types), name (a customer, job, vendor, employee or other name; part of a name finds every match), number (document or check number), amount (exact, or amount_from/amount_to on the total), date_from/date_to, memo text and account. Each row gives date, type, number, name, account, memo, amount and status (open, paid, posted, closed or void) with the id and the `show_command` that opens it, sorted by date then number. Voided documents are included unless include_voided is false; deleted ones are not. Use this first when asked to find, look up or locate a document, e.g. "the $412.50 check to Acme": types ["check"], name "Acme", amount "412.50".

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | ledger.read |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/transaction.find` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow transaction find --types '["check"]' --name Regional --amount 184.00 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --json`

### MCP

The same example as complete `bookflow_run` arguments:

```json
{"command": "transaction find", "input": {"types": ["check"], "name": "Regional", "amount": "184.00"}, "company": "Company ID or name"}
```

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `types` | `--types` | array[literal["invoice", "sales_receipt", "credit_memo", "statement_charge", "payment", "customer_refund", "estimate", "proposal", "work_order", "purchase_order", "item_receipt", "bill", "bill_payment", "vendor_credit", "check", "card_charge", "card_credit", "deposit", "transfer", "journal_entry", "sales_tax_payment", "sales_tax_adjustment", "inventory_adjustment"]] \| null | no | yes | null | Document types to search; omit for every type. invoice, sales_receipt, credit_memo, statement_charge, payment, customer_refund, estimate, proposal, work_order, purchase_order, item_receipt, bill, bill_payment, vendor_credit, check, card_charge, card_credit, deposit, transfer, journal_entry, sales_tax_payment, sales_tax_adjustment, inventory_adjustment. |
| `name` | `--name` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Customer, job, vendor, employee or other name, by id or full name; a name that is no party's exact name finds every party whose name contains it. A customer includes its jobs, and a merged-away name is found under the name it was merged into. |
| `name_type` | `--name-type` | literal["customer", "vendor", "employee", "other_name"] \| null | no | yes | null | Which list `name` is on, when the same name is on two. |
| `number` | `--number` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Document or check number, exact (letter case ignored). |
| `amount` | `--amount` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Exact document total, a decimal string such as "412.50". |
| `amount_from` | `--amount-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Smallest document total, inclusive. |
| `amount_to` | `--amount-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Largest document total, inclusive. |
| `date_from` | `--date-from` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Inclusive first document date, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `date_to` | `--date-to` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Inclusive last document date, YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `memo` | `--memo` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Text the memo contains (or a line's description, or an estimate's title); letter case ignored. |
| `account` | `--account` | string \| null | no | yes | null | Account ID or full name the document posts to; purchase orders, estimates, proposals and work orders post nothing and are left out when this is given. |
| `include_voided` | `--include-voided` | boolean | no | no | true | false leaves voided documents out. |
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 50 | minimum 1; maximum 200 |
| `cursor` | `--cursor` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/transaction.find`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
